entries.name: RHYTHM.elevation
entries.above: The rhythm added to the input's girdle above HT 25: elevation 0.05 deg/deg is Ludewig 2009's clavicle (+6 over the arc); the retraction is a fit of ours: Ludewig's mean over the three planes (+16 over the arc, about 0.12 deg/deg) spread by the plane, 0.06 in flexion to 0.18 in abduction (the paper: more retraction in abduction, up to 15 degrees more in the mid range).  No retraction is added where the dance pushes the shoulder forward (PROTRACTED_DEG, a smoothstep from 0).

entries.name: DOWN_ACC_MAX
entries.comment: units/s^2: the pelvis's downward acceleration, the dance's and the layer's together, at most this: the real g at 8 cm a unit (122.5). entries.name: HUMAN_CLOSING_FRAMES
entries.above: A spontaneous blink closes in 2 to 3 frames and opens in 4 to 7, 7 to 12 frames in all as the end of the opening is taken (Wu et al. 2014: 7.8 frames; Trutoiu et al. 2011: 9 frames measured most often, a character's blink most natural at 7 to 9 frames, less at 11 and 13); the opening is close to an exponential with a time constant of about 2 frames (Espinosa et al. 2020).  v7's shapes (CLOSING, OPENING: 7 to 10 frames) are kept; the lid stays shut a frame longer only one time in four (a spontaneous blink barely pauses shut: Malbouisson et al. 2010). Long blinks are a decided value.  No study measured singers' blinks; the long blinks of conversation (Homke et al. 2017, 2018) are a listener's, at the end of the speaker's turn, and no ground for a singer's.  Some blinks after a phrase (P_LONG["phrase_end"]) and where nothing is sung (P_LONG["rest"]) stay shut 3 to 4 frames, 10 to 11 frames in all: a character's blink looked most natural at 7 to 9 frames and already less so at 11 (Trutoiu et al. 2011), so they are kept short of 12; two are at least LONG_GAP frames apart (a review found four within 10 seconds in B2).

entries.above: ---- the hover (floaty, 2026-10-17) ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- No foot on the floor while the lower one is just over it (the trace's keys sit on a 0.3 unit grid: 2.4 cm; the dance's model has longer feet, so Rin's pointed feet stop short of the floor) and the pelvis does not fall: the body is held by nothing.  a05 s11's 'hover support' (no foot within 0.4 cm, one within 4 cm) is 8 % of the song in the MV (v9, balance-v3; 10 % in the trace) and 1.4 % [0.5, 2.2] in people (FineDance's near kinds, 62 sequences), runs of 6 frames or more 9.3 a minute against 0 [0, 1.2] (_spike/out/stage6/floaty/NOTES.md).  There the whole figure is lowered (the centre and both leg IKs by the same height: every joint's angle kept) until the lower shoe stands on the floor, the sink eased in and out over HOVER_EASE frames (lengthened, then lessened, where it would take the pelvis's fall past HOVER_ACC_BOUND, the balance layer's bound).  Putting the lower foot down alone straightened the knees (by up to 30 degrees in the song: a bent stance on the toes made straight), as the trace's longer feet would; so in the run the feet keep the dance's shape (no laying flat, no toes bent onto the floor, no heel turned: the layer takes them as in the air there), the sink alone brings the lower shoe down.  A run whose pelvis falls at least HOVER_FLIGHT_ACC over the run (a hop: in flight the body falls at gravity, 122.5 units/s^2 at 8 cm a unit), or faster than HOVER_ACC_BOUND on any frame of it (a hop whose take-off and landing in the run flatten the fit), keeps its height, and so does a run shorter than HOVER_MIN_RUN (a hover of a frame or two between steps: people have 1.4 % of such frames, runs of 6 frames or more not at all).  Only the frames where the lower shoe is held are taken: where it travels along the floor faster than HOVER_GLIDE it is a step's swing skimming the floor (the trace model's toe would not have stood there either), and the sink would drag the toe along the floor.

entries.above: ---- the landing (feet-landing, 2026-10-16) --------------------------------------------------------------------------- The sources and the measures are in _spike/out/stage6/feet_landing/NOTES.md and _spike/out/stage6/feet/RESEARCH.md (5). The human baseline (FineDance, the K-pop / choreography / jazz sequences, 62, the per-sequence medians' median): at a touchdown the ankle stands 3.1 cm [2.6, 3.5] over a flat foot's (96 % land toes first), comes down 2.0 cm [1.4, 2.5] in the next 0.2 s while the pelvis sinks 1.17 cm, so the hip joint's distance to the ankle hardly changes (-0.05 cm [-0.44, 0]) and the knee bends 0.3 degrees more; the heel is down a median 3 frames (0.1 s) after the touch, 61 % of them within 6 frames.  The research: in an ordinary landing the heel comes down some 40 ms after the forefoot (Puddle & Maulder 2013), the ankle dorsiflexing 9.8 degrees from the toe's touch to the heel's and 10 more by 150 ms (Fukano & Fukubayashi 2014); 7 of 11 landers put the heel down after the metatarsal heads, 4 absorbed the landing on the forefoot alone (Gross & Nelson 1988).  The MV's dance lands with the foot IK stopped on the floor, so the whole sink goes into the knee (7 degrees in 0.2 s).

entries.name: PACE.c

entries.name: FOLLOW_SCALE
entries.above: the follow (--follow; off by default): each finger reaches the shape its muscles take it to through the passive body's spring and damper (its omega and zeta between the open and the held hand), so a change comes 2 zeta / omega (= B / K) late.  --follow-scale multiplies that time (omega divided by it).  When on, the scale keeps half of the body's B / K: a shape's command is timed to the wrist's (in a throw the fingers start to open 4 ms after the wrist starts to flex, Hore, Ritchie & Watts 1999; moving the wrist and the fingers together pulls them in phase, the more the faster, Dounskaia 2000, 2009), and half gives 2.6 - 5.6 ms in a held shape, 5.7 - 12 ms in an open hand on Rin's fingers; on Hibikase's v8 the analysts' a09 from the wrist to the middle finger then reads +0.53 / +0.54 frames (the report's wrist, 手捩 in it), under the elbow -> wrist +0.56 / +0.60 (a lighter part drags less, Lasseter 1987).  1 is the whole B / K (+0.74 / +0.68).  Off by default because in a style near Hibikase's people's fingers do not trail the wrist by that measure (FineDance, 197 optically captured sequences: K-pop-like and street dance 0 or below, raw and through a zero-phase 6 Hz low-pass; all styles +0.04 / +0.06 raw, +0.10 / +0.16 at 6 Hz; BEAT's gestures at 120 Hz -11 / -5 ms with what is above 30 Hz taken out, the fingers ahead; _spike/out/stage6/fingers/research/R2_human_mocap.md and _spike/out/stage6/review_fingers_lag/REVIEW.md)

entries.name: REACH.band
entries.above: the hinges and the coupling undo a shape the trace made at the wrong joint (the thumbs of a heart bent sideways at their MP, a pinch made at the index's PIP, a fist hooked at the DIP); the finger goes back to the input's outline, carried by the joints that can move that way: a long finger's MP (flexion and sideways) and its PIP with the DIP in the coupling's band, the thumb's CMC (radial and palmar abduction) and its MP and IP (flexion).  A least-squares fit per frame (Gauss-Newton, the Jacobian by central differences, a step kept only where it lowers the cost): the distances of the finger's joints and tip from the input's (mm), each free angle's change from the hinged shape (reg mm per degree: among equal fits the smallest change), the DIP past the soft wall of the band (band mm per degree, where the input's PIP bends: the band does not let go when the fit opens the PIP) and an angle past the soft start of its range (rom mm per degree; the cap is the last step's)
